rationale: Interpret the public-contract execution for the first question (CheckRun c86ee7b6e6604a269dc8aff31adce625, fixed experiment ce111f77e8d4430ab1fca3ff482b3cd1-experiment, version 4): all four comparisons resolved - the leader-state and postponement premises hold and both witness assertions are violated - and the raw event stream shows the premise that previously had to be supplied, namely applied progress reported through Advance while the application is still applying the committed configuration change. The account's premise therefore moves from a fixture to a documented public sequence, the earlier fully-resolved basis stays as support for the forwarded path and the leave-joint variant, and the question's answered premise is replaced in the discriminator by the remaining open point.

investigations.discriminator: Whether the omission has consequences beyond the unanswered caller - for example an application that ties its own deadline to the read and re-issues it, or a caller that reuses one request context for several reads - and whether the postponed form exists for any read-only option other than ReadOnlySafe.

interpretations.rationale: The account now rests on a public-contract receipt for the premise and on the earlier fully-resolved receipt for the two completion paths. Source side: a leader postpones MsgReadIndex exactly when its configuration is not a singleton and no entry of its term is committed (raft.go:1354-1372); the only code that discharges the duty is releasePendingReadIndexMessages, called from the MsgAppResp commit path alone (raft.go:1550-1554), although switchToConfig also performs the term's first commit (raft.go:2013-2028) and the helper is guarded only by committedEntryInCurrentTerm() (raft.go:2127-2145); a postponed request is absent from readOnly.unconfirmedReads, so no heartbeat carries its context (read_only.go:93-101, raft.go:1600-1602). Receipt c86ee7b6e6604a269dc8aff31adce625 drives the decisive state through the Node interface: the application consumes the wrapped leader's Readys, writes entries and hard state, calls Advance while it is still applying the committed configuration change (permitted by node.go:166-187) so that applied progress through index 10 is reported with the tracker still holding voters=(1 2 3 4), campaigns through the Node interface and reaches StateLeader at term 2 with its term entry acknowledged only by voter 2 (parsed index 1 holds: state StateLeader, and the raw event carries last_index 11 with Match {1:11, 2:11, 3:0, 4:0}), then issues ReadIndex with context A through the Node interface and sees the request postponed (parsed index 2 holds: pending_reads 1, no ReadState delivered), and finally calls ApplyConfChange for the change it had already observed: the leader's commit advances 10 -> 11 with committed_entry_term 2, i.e. the release condition the helper is guarded by, while the postponed request stays held and no Ready delivers a ReadState for context A (parsed index 3: both witness assertions violated with a complete witness). What the earlier receipt a1859bb05261498c820729722eef035f adds is coverage of the two completion paths and the second configuration-change variant: the same omission for a local ReadState and for a forwarded request whose answer must be a MsgReadIndexResp, in both the removal and the leave-joint shapes, with the release controls holding when an unrelated entry is committed through the MsgAppResp path. The defect statement is unchanged and now rests on the documented client sequence rather than a supplied applied index: a request the leader accepted by postponing can remain unanswered across a commit of an entry of its own term when switchToConfig performs that commit, no periodic or acknowledgement path inside raft repairs it, and the answer that eventually arrives after an unrelated commit or a client retry carries a safe index taken at release time.

knowledge.assertion: A leader postpones MsgReadIndex exactly when the configuration is not a singleton and committedEntryInCurrentTerm() is false.
Postponed requests are released only from the MsgAppResp commit path.
switchToConfig can perform the term's first commit and does not release pendingReadIndexMessages.
A postponed request is not in readOnly.unconfirmedReads, so heartbeats cannot release it.
The applied progress report and the ApplyConfChange call are not ordered by the library's contract.

counterevidence: The controls hold in the earlier receipt (parsed indices 6, 14 and 23): an unrelated proposal committed through the MsgAppResp path releases the postponed request and the answer is delivered, so the release mechanism is intact and the omission is specific to the switchToConfig commit path.

The Node.ReadIndex contract tells callers that read index requests can be lost without notice and that retries are their duty (node.go:218-224), so a retrying client is not blocked; the observation is an unanswered admissible request rather than a permanent client-visible outage.

The reachable prefix relies on documented application latitude - reporting applied progress before finishing the entries of a previous Ready (node.go:166-178) and calling ApplyConfChange later than that report (node.go:179-187) - and this receipt shows that sequence is reachable through the public interface, so the premise no longer depends on a supplied fixture; the unanswered request is not caused by that latitude, only the reachability of the state is.
The postponed form exists only for ReadOnlySafe: the lease-based branch answers from the leader's own commit index without postponing (raft.go:2146-2166), so that option cannot exhibit this omission.
limitations: The comparison holds the applied configuration change to be the one that first makes a current-term entry committable; a leader that had already committed any entry of its term answers later requests normally (committedEntryInCurrentTerm() is true, so nothing is postponed).

The public-contract harness drives the wrapped leader against bare raft followers, so the followers' Ready/Advance duties are exercised only implicitly (their acknowledgements are delivered or held by the harness) and both run in one process.

No state machine was run, so the consequence measured is the unanswered request itself (no ReadState, no MsgReadIndexResp). The safe-but-late index of the eventual answer follows from the contract, not from a served value in the receipt.
The reachability without the documented latitude is not measured: this basis demonstrates one documented sequence, not that no other (or no simpler) sequence reaches the state.
interpretations.joint_history: The two receipts belong to the same question and cover complementary parts of one defect. The earlier basis (a1859bb05261498c820729722eef035f) drives bare raft instances and its prefix supplies the applied index as a fixture; it covers the local ReadState and forwarded MsgReadIndexResp paths plus the leave-joint configuration variant, with release controls. This basis (c86ee7b6e6604a269dc8aff31adce625) wraps the leader, drives the premise through Readys, Advance and ApplyConfChange, and covers the local ReadState path with the same fixture values (ten term-1 entries, entry 10 removing voter 4, persisted commit 10) and the same fault model (voter 4 unreachable, voter 3's acknowledgements held). Its decisive indices 1, 2 and 3 correspond to the earlier basis's premises and witness, so the two receipts agree on the behaviour and the later one replaces the supplied premise rather than changing the finding.
